items.stem: In market sizing, SOM (serviceable obtainable market) represents the share that:

options.text: Everyone in the world could theoretically buy
options.rationale: That describes TAM, the total addressable market.

options.text: You can realistically win in a defined period
options.rationale: Correct: SOM is the reachable, winnable portion in practice.

options.text: Your segment could buy if you reached all of it
options.rationale: That is SAM, the serviceable available market.
SOM is about what you can obtain, not what rivals hold.

items.explanation: Correct: SOM is the reachable, winnable portion in practice.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A 'beachhead' market-entry approach means first targeting:

options.text: As many segments as possible at once
options.rationale: That is the opposite of a focused beachhead.

options.text: One narrow segment you can win and build from
options.rationale: Correct: a beachhead concentrates resources on a winnable first segment.
Size alone does not define a beachhead.

options.text: Whichever region has the lowest taxes
options.rationale: Tax is one factor, not the beachhead logic.

items.explanation: Correct: a beachhead concentrates resources on a winnable first segment.

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine barriers to entering a new market? (Select TWO)

options.text: Strong incumbent brands with loyal customers
options.rationale: Correct: entrenched brands make it costly to win customers.
Correct: regulatory hurdles raise the cost and time to enter.

options.text: A large and growing addressable market
options.rationale: A growing market is an attraction, not a barrier.
Easy distribution lowers, not raises, the barrier.
